objective: Minimise total Euclidean route distance over all vehicles. Travel time equals distance (speed 1), so the clock and the length are the same quantity up to waiting.
constraints: every customer served exactly once across all routes
sum of demand on a route <= capacity 40
arrival at a customer <= its tw_end; early arrival waits until tw_start; service takes 0.2
every route's total Euclidean length, depot legs included, <= route_limit 3.0
every route starts and ends at the depot; the vehicle must be back by depot_end 3.0

state_variables.name: visited
state_variables.meaning: customers already served on the current route

state_variables.name: load
state_variables.meaning: demand carried on the current route, against capacity 40

state_variables.name: current_time
state_variables.meaning: clock along the route: max(arrival, tw_start) + 0.2

state_variables.name: current_length
state_variables.meaning: Euclidean length driven so far on the current route

state_variables.name: current_node
state_variables.meaning: last node of the partial route; 0 is the depot

masking_rules.name: unvisited
masking_rules.condition: a customer that is already served on this route, or at all, cannot be selected again

masking_rules.name: capacity
masking_rules.condition: load + demand[j] <= 40 for the candidate j

masking_rules.name: time_window
masking_rules.condition: max(current_time + d(i,j), tw_start[j]) <= tw_end[j]; a late arrival is infeasible, an early one waits

masking_rules.name: route_limit
masking_rules.condition: current_length + d(i,j) + d(j,0) <= 3.0, so the route can still return to the depot

masking_rules.name: depot_always_allowed
masking_rules.condition: node 0 is never masked, so a state with no legal customer stays escapable

feasibility_checklist: after every insertion, confirm the vehicle can still return to the depot within 3.0
confirm the sum of distances along the route (depot legs included) is <= 3.0
confirm no customer is skipped and none is served twice
confirm the routes are written with depot legs: each starts and ends with 0

pomo_modification_plan.change: replace the capacity-only mask with the five masks above, including the route-limit and return-by-horizon lookaheads that use the return leg to the depot
carry current_time and current_length per rollout; advance time by max(arrival, tw_start) + 0.2 and length by the Euclidean leg
leave the architecture unchanged; the checkpoint pins the encoder input width
none for the training schedule; the variant lives in the environment

run_plan.check: five masks exist: unvisited, capacity, time window, route limit, return-by-horizon; the depot is never masked
current_time and current_length are updated per rollout from the instance values, not from constants
the training generator reads capacity, route limit and service time from the instance instead of hard-coding them
prints both contract lines and writes routes whose length each stay within 3.0

output_contract.initial_cost_regex: the initial process is successful, the initial cost is (\d+(?:\.\d+)?)
output_contract.best_cost_regex: the process is successful, the best cost is (\d+(?:\.\d+)?)

recommended_approach: Keep POMO's encoder and training loop. Move the variant into the environment: five masks (unvisited, capacity, time window, route limit, return-by-horizon) with the depot never masked, and carry the clock and the length as per-rollout state. The instance set is MVMoE's, so capacity 40, route limit 3.0 and service 0.2 must be read from the instance, not hard-coded.
risks: symmetrising or ignoring the depot return leg: a route that looks legal forward is often illegal once the return is added
hard-coding capacity or the route limit instead of reading them from the instance
masking the depot, which makes a dead-end state unescapable and shows up as a crash rather than a bad solution
tuning the training budget away from POMO's, which would invalidate the comparison with MVMoE
